results.name: apprun-render-help
results.output:
vc_render_tifxyz: Render volume data using segmentation surfaces

Usage:

Required arguments:
  -v [ --volume ] arg                   Local OME-Zarr volume directory, or a 
                                        remote OME-Zarr URL (http(s)://, s3://)
                                        to stream; remote chunks persist in the
                                        shared remote cache
  --scale arg                           Pixels per level-g voxel (Pg)
  -g [ --group-idx ] arg                OME-Zarr group index

Optional arguments:
  -h [ --help ]                         Show this help message
  -s [ --segmentation ] arg             Path to a single tifxyz segmentation 
                                        folder
  --cache-gb arg (=16)                  Zarr chunk cache size in GB
  --prefetch-remote                     With a remote --volume, fetch the 
                                        chunks this render reads into the 
                                        shared remote cache before rendering 
                                        instead of streaming them during the 
                                        render
  --remote-url arg                      [DEPRECATED] Same as passing the remote
                                        OME-Zarr URL as --volume
  --log-path arg                        Log all output to file instead of 
                                        stdout/stderr
  --timeout arg (=0)                    Kill process if not finished within N 
                                        minutes
  -n [ --num-slices ] arg (=1)          Number of slices to render
  --slice-step arg (=1)                 Spacing between slices along normal
  --accum arg (=0)                      Accumulation sub-step (0 = disabled)
  --accum-type arg (=max)               Reducer: max, mean, median, alpha, 
                                        beerlambert. max/mean/median only take 
                                        effect with --accum or 
                                        --composite-collapse; alpha and 
                                        beerlambert always collapse the band 
                                        into one composite image (see 
                                        --composite-collapse).
  --crop-x arg (=0)                     Crop X
  --crop-y arg (=0)                     Crop Y
  --crop-width arg (=0)                 Crop width
  --crop-height arg (=0)                Crop height
  --auto-crop                           Auto-crop to valid surface bbox
  --affine arg                          Affine JSON files (append :inv to 
                                        invert)
  --affine-invert arg                   0-based indices to invert
  --affine-transform arg                [DEPRECATED] Single affine JSON
  --invert-affine                       [DEPRECATED] Invert single affine
  --scale-segmentation arg (=1)         Scale segmentation
  --rotate arg (=0)                     Rotate output (0/90/180/270)
  --flip arg (=-1)                      Flip: 0=V, 1=H, 2=Both
  --flip-normals                        Negate surface normals (reverses slice 
                                        ordering along the normal)
  --surface-interpolation arg (=linear) Surface resampling: linear (bilinear 
                                        positions, nearest-neighbour normals) 
                                        or smooth/bicubic (Catmull-Rom 
                                        positions with normals differentiated 
                                        from the same basis). The source grid 
                                        is far coarser than the render, so 
                                        linear leaves the normal constant 
                                        across each grid cell and every offset 
                                        layer steps at the cell edges; smooth 
                                        removes those steps and the creases 
                                        between them, at ~3-5x the surface-warp
                                        cost (a few percent end to end).
  --zarr-output arg                     Output path for .zarr (optional)
  --zarr-compressor arg (=blosc)        Zarr compressor: blosc, zstd, gzip, 
                                        lz4, none
  --zarr-compression-level arg (=-1)    Zarr compression level (<=0 = 
                                        compressor default)
  --zarr-separator arg (=/)             Zarr chunk dimension separator: / or .
  --tif-output arg                      Output path for per-slice TIFFs 
                                        (optional)
  --quick-tif                           Fast TIF: PACKBITS + zero low nibble
  --flatten                             ABF++ flattening
  --flatten-iterations arg (=10)        ABF++ iterations
  --flatten-downsample arg (=1)         ABF++ downsample factor
  --alpha-min arg (=0)                  Alpha min (0-255)
  --alpha-max arg (=255)                Alpha max (0-255)
  --alpha-opacity arg (=230)            Alpha opacity (0-255)
  --alpha-cutoff arg (=9950)            Alpha cutoff (0-10000)
  --bl-extinction arg (=1.5)            Beer-Lambert extinction
  --bl-emission arg (=1.5)              Beer-Lambert emission
  --bl-ambient arg (=0.100000001)       Beer-Lambert ambient
  --iso-cutoff arg (=0)                 Highpass (0-255)
  --composite-start arg                 Composite start offset
  --composite-end arg                   Composite end offset
  --composite-collapse                  Collapse the sampled band into a single
                                        image using --accum-type as the reducer
                                        (max/mean/median, in addition to the 
                                        implicit alpha/beerlambert). The band 
                                        spans [--composite-start, 
                                        --composite-end] layers along the 
                                        normal at --slice-step spacing; use a 
                                        symmetric range (e.g. 
                                        --composite-start=-54 
                                        --composite-end=54) for a centered 
                                        projection.
  --num-parts arg (=1)                  Parts for multi-VM
  --part-id arg (=0)                    Part ID (0-indexed)
  --merge-tiff-parts                    Merge partial TIFFs from multi-VM 
                                        render
  --pyramid arg (=1)                    Build pyramid levels L1-L5 (default: 
                                        true)
  --resume                              Skip chunks that already exist on disk
  --pre                                 Create zarr + all level datasets
  --voxel-size arg                      Physical voxel size for OME-Zarr scale 
                                        metadata (reads from volume metadata if
                                        omitted)
  --voxel-unit arg (=nanometer)         Unit of the number given to 
                                        --voxel-size (nanometer, micrometer, 
                                        millimeter, meter). Sizes read from 
                                        volume metadata are always declared in 
                                        micrometer.

results.name: apprun-trim-usage
results.output:
usage: /workspace/villa-headless-evidence/squashfs-root/usr/bin/vc_tifxyz_trim <src tifxyz dir> [<dst tifxyz dir>]
  Crops x.tif/y.tif/z.tif and any sibling .tif channels (mask, etc.)
  to the bounding box of valid grid cells. Channels at integer multiples
  of the grid resolution are cropped in lockstep; channels with
  non-integer ratios are skipped.
  When <dst> is omitted or equal to <src>, the segment is replaced
  via a sibling temp dir + atomic rename.
